paraPsav.title: For VASPs
paraPsav.message: We deliver verifiable, explainable on-chain signals on source of funds, recent behavior, and wallet maturity so VASPs can strengthen risk assessment and monitoring within their own due-diligence framework.
paraPsav.problemBody: BCU Circular No. 2507 establishes the authorization regime and obligations for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs / PSAVs) in Uruguay. VASPs need stronger wallet risk assessment and monitoring. Part of that intelligence can come from verifiable on-chain signals.
paraPsav.problemClose: Walpulse addresses that need from the on-chain signals side, without assuming the formal obligations the regulation assigns to the VASP.

map.contribution: Good as signals (wash, circular, bot-like, mixing)

does: Produces on-chain reputation, maturity, and risk signals for wallets (A–F scale).
Delivers verifiable, explainable information (the recipient can audit how each grade was reached).
Especially covers: source of funds, recent behavior, multi-chain presence, and portfolio quality.
Serves as input so the VASP can enrich its own risk assessment and monitoring system.
doesNot: It does not perform KYC or identify the person behind the wallet.
It does not execute Travel Rule.
It does not report to UIAF.
It does not perform official list screening or freezing.
It does not make compliance decisions or classify customers into regulatory risk categories.
It does not produce the formal report or written examination the regulation requires from the VASP.
benefits: Structured on-chain evidence on source of funds and recent behavior.
Early detection of risk signals (mixing, wash trading, bot-like activity, anomalous concentrations).
Enrichment of the activity profile and risk-based approach with auditable data.
Traceability: Walpulse does not obfuscate; it classifies and makes behavior more visible.
Integration as input to the VASP’s own due-diligence process, without transferring regulatory responsibility.

nosotros.title: About
nosotros.intro: Walpulse grows out of concrete work in the Ethereum Uruguay ecosystem. It began as a hackathon project, became signals from an autonomous agent, and later an independent project delivering on-chain reputation intelligence for wallets.
nosotros.originBody: At the Ethereum Uruguay Hackathon 2026 (3rd edition), the ORIGO project — verifiable analysis of wallet source of funds — won 1st place in the Startup category. The final pitch and awards ceremony took place at Blockchain Summit Global 2026 (Montevideo).
nosotros.originBody2: It did not stay a demo: source-of-funds signals were integrated into production as Walcert Origins. Walpulse is the independent project that continues and expands that approach.
nosotros.originTeam: Hackathon team (public coverage): Jair Valenzuela and Rodrigo Médica.

jair.name: Ibzan Jair Valenzuela Suarez
jair.bio: Data Engineer with over 12 years of experience in databases, data warehousing, and large-scale data transformation. He leads Walpulse product vision and the definition of on-chain reputation signals.

carolina.name: Carolina Rodriguez Conde
carolina.bio: Lawyer graduated from Universidad Católica del Uruguay, current lead of the legal roundtable of Cámara Blockchain del Uruguay and collaborator with Ethereum Uruguay; her professional path has specialized in the convergence of law and technology, focusing on Web3 ecosystems and normative regulation. She has extensive experience in legal compliance, advising on comprehensive security standards (such as ISO 27001), legal structuring of smart contracts, and intellectual property protection. Her track record designing legal architectures for innovative technology projects provides the solid normative base that enables transforming on-chain data analysis into institutional regulatory intelligence and risk-mitigation tools.

origins.lead: We look up origin transactions and analyze the provenance, validity, and trustworthiness of the wallet’s funds. That lets us create some of the following signals:

bullets.categories: Origin categories (CEX, bridge, mixer, OFAC, airdrop, organic…)
bullets.mixerOrSanctionsExposure: Exposure to wallets labeled as mixers or wallets flagged by sanctions

origins.depthNote: The number of networks and origin transactions varies depending on the type of analysis requested, starting in the basic version at 2 networks and 100 origin transactions and reaching more than +10 networks and 500 transactions in the expert version. Standard/Expert also add funder risk screening (provenance context, not a second Origins run).
origins.whyBody: The origin of funds is one of the first questions when evaluating a wallet. Understanding where the first funds came from helps define a clear context for a wallet’s behavior and lets the signal recipient assess, within their own decision framework, the level of trust they will have when interacting with that wallet.

activity.lead: We analyze a recent day window and, based on on-chain inflow and outflow transactions, create the following signals:

bullets.counterparties: Unique counterparties and concentration of movements
bullets.patterns: Possible interactions labeled as wash / circular / bot-like

activity.depthNote: The number of networks and the Activity window vary by analysis type: Basic (top 2 networks, last 15 days), Standard (top 5, 45 days), and Expert (top 10, 90 days). In Expert, a light analysis is also run on the 5 wallets with the most interaction.
activity.whyBody: A wallet’s activity lets the recipient understand the wallet’s behavior in daily transactions, helping assess the reputation and trust profile that can be formed about a wallet and even detect early warnings of risks that could otherwise remain hidden.

multichain.lead: Using professional tools, we run a discovery process across the networks where the wallet is active, enabling some of the following signals:

bullets.activeWindows: Networks active in the last 30 or 90 days

multichain.depthNote: The number of networks covered by the discovery process varies depending on the type of analysis requested, starting at 15 networks in the basic version and reaching more than 100 networks in the expert version.
multichain.whyBody: This first signal correctly identifies the universe of networks that should be analyzed in the following signals. It also gives the signal recipient a complete map of all activity executed by a wallet.

portfolio.lead: A multi-chain analysis of the wallet is performed, assessing not only economic composition but also fund quality. That lets us offer some of the following signals:
portfolio.depthNote: We run an analysis using professional tools that measure a wallet’s portfolio across more than 38 chains (including Solana). Portfolio is included in Standard and Expert; not in Basic.
portfolio.whyBody: It creates a complete view of the wallet’s portfolio, the total economic value, and the health of the holdings — a general snapshot that helps the recipient understand the type of wallet they will interact with.

tierNote.multichain: Multichain is included in Basic, Standard, and Expert; networks and intensity scale with depth.

intro.title: What is Walpulse?
intro.body: We produce a wallet analysis at three depths: Basic, Standard, or Expert, based on on-chain signals (ecosystem presence, source of funds, recent activity, and — in Standard/Expert — portfolio). Coming soon: Risk Engine — a client-parametrizable score on those signals.
intro.explainLead: The analysis is not a black box, nor a final rating. We prioritize that the recipient understands the signals tied to each element analyzed and, based on them, makes informed decisions when interacting with the wallet.
intro.explainGoal: Our goal is that the recipient understands:

explainPoints.variables: Which blockchain signals were read for each element
explainPoints.factors: How risk or maturity factors were calculated

intro.explainImageAlt: Explainability: the analysis is not a black box

riesgo.intro: Configure your risk matrices: rules over the analysis signals, versioned, with an explicit rollout to sandbox or production.
riesgo.sinEvaluadorHint: The evaluator is not in production yet: this screen configures the matrix, it does not simulate a wallet's score.
riesgo.catalogoIntro: The signals the analysis computes, available as conditions in your matrix rules.
riesgo.matricesEmptyBody: A matrix groups rules over the analysis signals. Create the first one, add rules to its draft version and publish it when it is ready.
riesgo.nuevaIntro: The name is for your team; the identifier is used in the API and must be unique within your client.
riesgo.slugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Example: onboarding-matrix.
riesgo.cicloHint: Every version defines a 0-100 risk score and each rule adds points. Rules are edited in a draft; to publish it, its enabled rules must add up to exactly 100. A matrix has a single current version: publishing the next one turns the previous into history. To test without touching production, duplicate the matrix and point the sandbox at that copy.
riesgo.versionesEmpty: This matrix has no versions. Create the first one to start adding rules.
riesgo.crearVersionHint: The new version starts as a draft with a copy of the latest version's rules, so you can adjust without entering them again.
riesgo.publicarObsoleta: A newer version is already current
riesgo.publicarReemplaza: Publishing v{version} turns v{vigente} into history.
riesgo.publicarPrimera: Publishing v{version} makes it the current version of this matrix.
riesgo.matrizSinVigente: Publish a version to deploy it
riesgo.sinOtraMatriz: You need another matrix to copy into
riesgo.duplicarMatrizIntro: The copy arrives with every version as a draft and no deployment, so you can test without touching this matrix.
riesgo.reglasSinPuntos: No points left: lower another rule's points to add or duplicate.
riesgo.versionCongeladaHint: This version is published and its rules are frozen. To change them, create a new version.
riesgo.reglasEmpty: This version has no rules yet.
riesgo.reglasEmptyPublicada: It was published with no rules.
riesgo.puntosSobrepasa: You are {puntos} points over the budget of 100.
riesgo.puntosCompletos: All 100 points are assigned: the version can be published.
riesgo.puntosFaltanPublicar: To publish, the enabled rules must add up to 100: {puntos} missing.
riesgo.operadorHint: Only conditions compatible with the signal type are offered.
riesgo.valoresLibresHint: This signal does not declare a fixed list, so values are typed by hand.
